interpretation.diagram_classification: cosmological / natural-philosophical diagram of correspondences (microcosm–macrocosm; elements, seasons, humours, qualities)
interpretation.interpretation: The diagram is a concentric scheme of correspondences between the world (mundus), the year (annus) and the human being (homo), as the central text states. The outer ring gives the four elements (IGNIS, AER, AQUA, TERRA) together with their paired qualities (calidus/calidur, siccus/secca, humidus, frigidus/frigidur). The inner ring gives the four seasons (AESTAS, uer, hiemps, autumnus) and the four humours (colera, sanguis, flegma or humor with hiemps, melancolia). The interlocking coloured arcs link each element to its two qualities and to the season and humour that share them. Fire is hot and dry and matches summer and choler. Air is hot and moist and matches spring and blood. Water is cold and moist and matches winter and phlegm. Earth is cold and dry and matches autumn and black bile. The three levels (cosmos, time, human body) are thus presented as parallel structures governed by the same four-fold scheme. The diagram follows the Isidorian and Bedan tradition of early medieval computus and natural-philosophy manuscripts, and is of the type found in copies of Isidore's De natura rerum.
interpretation.evidence: Written in the diagram: the red central text "mundus / annus / homo"; the red labels IGNIS, AER, TERRA and the bottom red text (read as aqua when rotated); the season labels AESTAS, uer, hiemps and autumnus; the humour labels colera, sanguis, melancolia and humor/hiemps; and the quality words calidus, siccus, humidus and frigidus. These words cover the standard fourfold correspondences. Visible: the concentric structure, with elements outermost, seasons and humours inside and the central text in the middle. The interlocking yellow, orange and blue-grey arcs bind adjacent labels into pairs. External knowledge: the standard medieval doctrine of the four elements, qualities, humours and seasons, and the Isidorian tradition of such diagrams. Cautions about Step 1: the lower-left compartment reads humor / hiemps, which is probably a mis-expansion of flegma, so the reading is uncertain. "secca" and "calidur" are probably siccus and calidus with a final-letter ambiguity. Entries 4 and 7 treat two compartments both as "secca", but the distinction is unclear. The red lower text is rendered "aqua" only by rotation. Some Step 1 predicates ("inside" for text in segments) are approximate, and the assignment of each outer label to specific inner labels rests on the arc pattern, which is hard to follow.

interpretation.diagram_classification: colour-coded structural scheme (arcs as relational links)
interpretation.interpretation: The colours of the arcs (blue-grey, yellow, orange-red) and their crossing pattern work as a system for linking opposite and adjacent terms: shared qualities are joined by arcs of the same curve. The four lobes around the central text mark the four seasons and humours as parts of one closed cycle, and the four outer compartments mark the elements. The circular form suggests the cyclical, unified character of cosmos, year and human body.
interpretation.evidence: Visible: each long arc runs continuously from the outer ring into the inner ring and crosses others. The short blue-grey arcs separate the paired inner compartments, such as AESTAS / colera and humor / hiemps. The rotated text at the bottom suggests the diagram was meant to be read from several orientations, or was laid out around the centre. External knowledge supports reading this as a relational device, but the exact meaning of each colour is not clear from the image and may be only a scribal or decorative choice, so certainty is lowered.
